The [[1964 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the IX Olympic Winter Games, were an international winter [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Innsbruck]], Austria, from 29 January to 9 February.<ref>{{cite web |title=Innsbruck 1964 Olympic Winter Games {{!}} Alpine Skiing, Ice Hockey & Bobsleigh |url=https://www.britannica.com/event/Innsbruck-1964-Olympic-Winter-Games |website=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] |access-date=15 January 2025 |language=en |archive-date=27 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180627174839/https://www.britannica.com/event/Innsbruck-1964-Olympic-Winter-Games |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="IOC 1964 Winter Games">{{cite web |title=Innsbruck 1964 Winter Olympics – Athletes, Medals & Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/innsbruck-1964 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=14 January 2025 |archive-date=26 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240926064829/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/innsbruck-1964 |url-status=live }}</ref> A total of 1,091 athletes representing 36 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated,<ref name="IOC 1964 Winter Games" /> including [[India at the 1964 Winter Olympics|India]],<ref>{{cite web |title=India – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/india |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130225855/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/india |archive-date=2024-11-30 |url-status=dead |access-date=14 January 2025}}</ref> [[Mongolia at the 1964 Winter Olympics|Mongolia]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Mongolia – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/mongolia |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130224929/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/mongolia |archive-date=2024-11-30 |url-status=dead |access-date=14 January 2025}}</ref> and [[North Korea at the 1964 Winter Olympics|North Korea]], who took part in the Winter Games for the first time.<ref name="IOC NK">{{cite web |title=DPR Korea – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/dpr-korea |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006042817/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/dpr-korea |archive-date=2024-10-06 |url-status=dead |access-date=14 January 2025}}</ref> The games featured 34 events in 6 [[Winter Olympic sports|sports]] across 10 disciplines,<ref>{{cite web |title=Factsheet: The Winter Olympic Games |url=https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |date=2024-06-20 |access-date=15 January 2025 |archive-date=11 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240711124443/http://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Olympedia">{{cite web |title=1964 Innsbruck Winter Games |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/37 |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=14 January 2025 |archive-date=4 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250104025334/http://www.olympedia.org/editions/37 |url-status=live }}</ref> including the Olympic debut of [[Luge at the Winter Olympics|Luge]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lyfe: Olympic history, rules, latest updates and upcoming events for the Olympic sport |url=https://olympics.com/en/sports/luge/ |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=14 January 2025 |archive-date=7 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207112833/https://olympics.com/en/sports/Luge/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Athletes representing 14 NOCs received at least one medal, with 11 NOCs winning at least one gold medal.<ref name="IOC medal table" /> Athletes from the [[Soviet Union at the 1964 Winter Olympics|Soviet Union]] won the most gold medals, with 11, and most overall medals, with 25.<ref name="IOC medal table" /> The Netherlands won their first gold medal at the Winter Games, doing so in the women’s figure skating individual event,<ref>{{cite web |title=Netherlands – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/netherlands |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006044154/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/netherlands |archive-date=2024-10-06 |url-status=dead |access-date=14 January 2025}}</ref> while North Korea won their first medal of any kind, taking silver in [[Speed skating at the 1964 Winter Olympics – Women's 3000 metres|women's 3,000 metres speed skating]].<ref name="IOC NK" /> Soviet speed skater [[Lidiya Skoblikova]] won four gold medals which was both the most gold and overall medals among individual participants.<ref name="Olympedia" />

==Medal table==
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympics 2024 medal table: How every nation stands in Paris |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |website=[[The Independent]] |date=24 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725050134/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |archive-date=25 July 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=25 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us |date=10 August 2024 |archive-date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

At the 1964 Winter Olympics, athletes were tied in three events. In the [[Speed skating at the 1964 Winter Olympics – Women's 3000 metres|women's 3000 metres speed skating]] and [[Alpine skiing at the 1964 Winter Olympics – Women's giant slalom|women's giant slalom]] events there were two-way ties for second, which resulted in two silver medals and no bronze medals being awarded in each event.<ref>{{cite web |title=Innsbruck 1964 3000m women Results – Olympic speed-skating |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/innsbruck-1964/results/speed-skating/3000m-women |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203150933/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/innsbruck-1964/results/speed-skating/3000m-women |archive-date=2024-12-03 |url-status=live |access-date=14 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Innsbruck 1964 giant slalom women Results – Olympic speed-skating |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/innsbruck-1964/results/alpine-skiing/giant-slalom-women |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250121165533/https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/innsbruck-1964/results/alpine-skiing/giant-slalom-women |archive-date=2025-01-21 |url-status=live |access-date=14 January 2025}}</ref> In the [[Speed skating at the 1964 Winter Olympics – Men's 500 metres|men's 500 metres speed skating]] event there was a three-way tie for second, which resulted in three silver medals and no bronze medal being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Innsbruck 1964 500m men Results – Olympic speed-skating |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/innsbruck-1964/results/speed-skating/500m-men |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=14 January 2025 |archive-date=20 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920060933/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/innsbruck-1964/results/speed-skating/500m-men |url-status=live }}</ref>
